subject: Private Offer - 3yr prepay: phasing, escrow holdback & ramp questions
messages:
From: Oliver Finch <oliver.finch@nexacloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@nexacloud.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T09:12:00Z
Subject: Private Offer: 3-year prepay — phasing & credit holdback

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the call this morning. NexaCloud is interested in moving to a marketplace private offer for Redwood for a 3-year committed prepay. A few items we need clarity on before we route to procurement:

- Can Redwood support a phased prepay schedule through the marketplace (year-by-year invoicing) with an overall 3-year commitment?
- Does Redwood support placing a percentage of credits in escrow (holdback) for operational creditability checks for the first 12 months? If so, what's the typical percentage and release cadence?
- How do you handle unused credits at each anniversary — true-up vs rollover? We have internal policy preferring limited rollover.

I've attached our current SOW and a short forecast. Procurement will want a term sheet showing discount schedule, true-up mechanics, and any escrow/holdback wording. Can you loop in pricing and finance folks?

Attachments: NexaCloud_MA_SOW_v1.pdf

Cheers,
Oliver Finch
Head of Cloud Procurement
NexaCloud
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Finch <oliver.finch@nexacloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Private Offer: 3-year prepay — phasing & credit holdback

Hi Oliver — thanks for the note and the SOW. Looping in Marissa from Sales Ops to help align the offer and Rishi from Revenue Ops will pick up finance-level details. A few quick answers and clarifying asks:

- We can do a marketplace private offer that phases billing year-by-year while keeping a contractual 3-year commitment. The marketplace will still surface a single private-offer agreement but invoicing can be configured as annual prepaids tied to the commitment schedule.
- Escrow/holdback is possible; common structures are 5–15% holdback released either quarterly or at a 12-month anniversary depending on customer risk profile and consumption predictability.
- For unused credits we typically offer an annual true-up at the anniversary with limited rollover allowed by exception. We can include a capped rollover (eg, 10% of the prior year) if that helps.

Two clarifying asks for your team:
1) Can you send a year-by-year consumption expectation (percent of total committed consumption by year)?
2) Do you need credits to be refundable or purely refundable via offset against future consumption?

Once we have those, Rishi will propose a draft term sheet and discount schedule. Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Cloud Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Oliver Finch <oliver.finch@nexacloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@nexacloud.com>, procurement@nexacloud.com
Date: 2027-08-23T08:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Private Offer: 3-year prepay — phasing & credit holdback

Karthik — thanks, that helps. Per procurement, our target ramp looks like this:

- Year 1: 30% of total committed consumption
- Year 2: 40%
- Year 3: 30%

We expect Year 1 to be weighted to the latter half of the year as we complete integration. Important notes from procurement:
- We prefer true-up at the anniversary over unconditional rollover.
- If there is any rollover, cap should be 10% and capped credits expire at the end of year 3.
- Escrow: procurement is proposing a 10% holdback released at 12 months; they are open to shortening to 6 months if it mitigates go-live risk.

Attached: NexaCloud_consume_forecast.xlsx

Can Rishi propose specific discount tiers for the three-year structure and confirm whether the 10% holdback can be managed via marketplace escrow or needs a separate escrow arrangement?

Regards,
Oliver
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Finch <oliver.finch@nexacloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-24T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Private Offer: 3-year prepay — phasing & credit holdback

Oliver — appreciate the forecast, that clarifies consumption shape. Proposed term sheet summary below (draft):

- Commitment: 3-year total commitment payable as annual prepay installments via Azure private offer. Each installment invoiced at the start of the year.
- Discount: 18% off list for the full 3-year commit (applies pro rata each invoice).
- Escrow/Holdback: 10% of each annual installment to be held in marketplace escrow and released at the 12-month anniversary for that installment unless a material compliance issue is detected.
- True-up: Annual true-up at each anniversary; unused credits may rollover up to 10% of that year (expires at end of year 3).
- Termination: Standard marketplace private-offer termination language with mutual cure period.

Notes and options: if NexaCloud prefers a shorter escrow period (6 months), we can accommodate by reducing escrow from 10% to 7% to balance vendor risk. Also open to a staggered release (quarterly 25% releases) if that maps better to your SSO/eng ramp.

Attached: Redwood_PrivateOffer_TermSheet_v3.pdf
DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcd-1234
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345

If that structure is acceptable we can issue a private offer draft and route to your procurement for signature. Would NexaCloud prefer a single exec-signoff call or separate procurement + finance sessions?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Oliver Finch <oliver.finch@nexacloud.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@nexacloud.com>
Date: 2027-08-25T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Private Offer: 3-year prepay — phasing & credit holdback

Rishi, Karthik — thanks for the draft. Procurement has reviewed and is largely aligned. Two requests before we sign:

1) Remove the rollover cap language and allow unused credits to roll up to 15% in Year 2 only (procurement will accept 0% beyond Year 2).
2) Shorten the escrow release to 6 months (the security team will accept this if Redwood reduces the holdback to 7%).

If you can reflect those two changes in the term sheet we will route to the CFO for exec sign-off. Let's set up a short call to finalize: I can do Friday 09:00–11:00 BST or Monday 14:00–16:00 BST. Karthik, can you coordinate?

Oliver Finch
Head of Cloud Procurement
NexaCloud
